Let $K$ be a field. A *central simple $K$-algebra* is a **finite-dimensional**, associative unital $K$-algebra $A$ with centre $K$ and no nonzero proper two-sided ideals. Its *degree* is $\sqrt{\dim_K A}$, an integer. The *opposite algebra* $A^{opp}$ has the same underlying space and reversed multiplication. Two central simple algebras are *Brauer equivalent* when matrix algebras of suitable sizes over them are isomorphic; $\operatorname{Br}(K)$ is the group of Brauer equivalence classes under tensor product. For a separable closure $K^{sep}$, $G_K=\operatorname{Gal}(K^{sep}/K)$, and $\mathrm{PGL}_d(K^{sep})=\mathrm{GL}_d(K^{sep})/(K^{sep})^\times$ with its natural Galois action, $H^1(G_K,\mathrm{PGL}_d(K^{sep}))$ denotes **non-abelian** continuous cohomology, a pointed set of 1-cocycles modulo conjugate coboundaries.

**Statement (source hypotheses preserved):**
Let $A$ be a finite central simple algebra over $K$. Then
$$
\begin{matrix}
A \otimes_K A^{opp} & \longrightarrow & \text{End}_K(A) \\
\ a \otimes a' & \longmapsto & (x \mapsto a x a')
\end{matrix}
$$
is an isomorphism of algebras over $K$.

**Typed interpretation:** The claim is interpreted using the preceding explicit definitions; retain exactly the original assumptions and conclusion.
